analysis.title: Market Pulse, November 2026 (SAS Market Strategy)
key_insights: Global growth is supported by corporate and household balance sheets, AI investment and fiscal cushions, which offset tighter monetary policy and higher commodity prices. GSAM expects 2027 growth near 2% in the US and above 1% in Europe and Japan.

The FOMC has telegraphed rate hikes at every other meeting. GSAM expects a hike in December, with March highly data dependent. If energy and tariff impulses roll off and inflation normalizes, the Fed may hold at 4.0-4.25%. If price pressures broaden, it may have to hike.
GSAM expects the ECB to deliver one more hike in December, taking the policy rate to a peak of 2.75%.

On the election cycle, GSAM focuses on what a win changes rather than who wins. A divided US government likely means gridlock. Upcoming elections in Spain, France and Italy put fiscal risk in focus, and fractured parliaments are less likely to address debt burdens. Government bond yields may stay elevated, as seen recently in French OATs.

Earnings growth has been exceptional in 2026, boosted by AI investment and higher energy prices. GSAM expects it to decelerate in 2027 but still support equities, and notes markets have historically rallied for years past peak earnings growth while becoming more idiosyncratic. Focus is expected to shift to value capture, quality revenues and balance sheet strength.

Higher rates have increased scrutiny of AI capex funding needs, causing greater dispersion and spread widening across the AI complex. GSAM remains cautious on IG tech but sees scope for a near-term reversal in HY after the recent selloff. Credit fundamentals are supportive and Q4 supply is expected to slow.

Base case is that energy prices moderate as supply and demand normalize and the risk premium recedes. Upside risks are a Middle East re-escalation or a colder than expected winter. GSAM sees upward pressure on copper (electrification, data centers and energy security against constrained mine supply) and on gold (robust central bank demand).

Global equities have been resilient as strong earnings offset energy market shocks. GSAM expects this diversification to keep delivering in 2027 with AI, defense and economic security themes intact. EM multiples are cheaper than they have been about 90% of the time over the last 20 years.

EM earnings strength is led by AI infrastructure and the three main hardware providers, with growth potential in specialized AI supply chains (chip inputs, testing, packaging, distribution). Commodity and consumer themes add breadth, and EM annualized EPS growth from 2005 to 2025 was just 3%.

Japan and Europe have been strong beneath the surface, with the median stock beating the median US stock. Europe's strength reflects limited tech concentration and benefits from higher rates, infrastructure spend, energy prices and higher dividend yields. Japan benefits from AI investment, defense and infrastructure spend and domestic fiscal impulse.

Dispersion has risen across global markets, with the gap between top and bottom performers over 400% in EM and 200% in DM. GSAM favors active management in EM (1,165 companies across 24 countries) and sees alpha potential in DM given high median stock returns and low cross-stock correlations.

Possible re-escalation in the Middle East is an upside risk to energy prices.
